content.text: {"relation":"DIVERGENT","consensus_summary":"All three blind responses converge on the same core: 'the Way' is primarily Jesus Christ himself as the exclusive path of access to God the Father and salvation (John 14:6; Heb 10:19-20), fused with the Acts usage of 'the Way' as the earliest name for the Christian movement. The moral/conduct sense (way of the righteous, walking in God's commandments, the two ways) is uniformly listed only as a common secondary/alternative sense, treated as feeding into or subordinate to the christological identification.","book_summary":"The book identifies 'the way' as covenant conduct — the walk: a manner of life in faithfulness to God's covenant, grounded in Jeremiah 6:16 ('ask for the old paths... walk therein') and Matthew 7:14 (the narrow way leading to life). Its common-view note explicitly flags 'Jesus Himself as the one way to the Father; the narrow way against the broad' as what is commonly taught, signaling that the book's own identification departs from that christological reading.","consensus_core_identification":"'The Way' = the person of Jesus Christ as the sole means of access to God/salvation (with the Acts community-name usage presupposing that titular sense).","book_core_identification":"'The way' = covenant conduct, i.e., the walk of covenant faithfulness — a manner of life, not a person.","core_relation":"CONTRADICTS","extension_relation":"PARTIAL_RECLASSIFICATION","boundary_disagreement":"The book takes what the consensus treats as a secondary ethical sense (Ps 1, Prov 4, Deut 5:33, Matt 7:13-14) and makes it the primary and controlling identification, while demoting the consensus's central christological referent (John 14:6; Heb 10:19-20; Acts titular usage) to a 'commonly taught' view it sets aside. Cases like Matt 7:14 are retained but reclassified from a Christ-centered narrow-way reading to a covenant-conduct reading; Jer 6:16's 'old paths' are added as paradigm cases.","material_contradiction":"The consensus says the symbol's central referent is a person — Christ himself as the way to the Father. The book says the referent is a pattern of behavior — covenant conduct, the walk. A person and a manner of life are different referents; the book's common-view note frames the personal-christological identification as the merely 'commonly taught' view it replaces. Accepting 'covenant conduct' as the core meaning requires rejecting 'Jesus Himself as the one way' as the core meaning, even though the conduct sense appears among the consensus's acknowledged secondary alternatives.","rationale":"Both axes point the same direction. At the core, the book substitutes covenant conduct for the person of Christ as the symbol's identification, and its own common-view note marks the christological reading as the view it departs from — that is replacement of the central referent, not boundary adjustment. At the extension, the book keeps some consensus cases (Matt 7:14) but reclassifies them under conduct and elevates OT walking-in-the-way texts (Jer 6:16) to paradigm status, while the consensus's anchor texts (John 14:6, Heb 10:20, Acts) drop out of the printed basis entirely. Because the conduct meaning is present in the consensus as a listed alternative, this is not NOVEL; because the central identification is replaced rather than narrowed, it is DIVERGENT rather than REFINED.","citation_support":"PARTIAL","strongest_objection":"All three consensus responses list the moral/conduct sense ('way of the righteous,' walking in God's commandments) as a common alternative, so one could argue the book merely re-weights an acknowledged layered sense — a boundary/emphasis shift within the same semantic family, which would make REFINED the correct verdict rather than DIVERGENT.","confidence":"medium"}
